recipes.name: High-Fiber Millet Upma with Mixed Vegetables
recipes.health_benefit: This recipe is rich in complex carbohydrates and fiber from millet and vegetables, which can help in managing blood glucose levels and supporting healthy digestion. It's also low in saturated fat, benefiting LDL management.

ingredients.item: Mixed vegetables (carrots, peas, beans, bell peppers)

instructions: Dry roast millet in a pan until fragrant, set aside.
Heat oil in the same pan, add mustard seeds and urad dal. Once spluttering, add curry leaves, green chilies, grated ginger, and chopped onion. Sauté until onion is translucent.
Add chopped mixed vegetables and turmeric powder. Sauté for 3-5 minutes until vegetables are slightly tender.
Add water and salt, bring to a boil. Gradually add the roasted millet, stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Cover and cook on low heat for 10-12 minutes, or until water is absorbed and millet is cooked. Fluff with a fork.
Stir in lemon juice and garnish with fresh coriander leaves before serving.

recipes.name: Omega-3 Rich Mackerel Fish Curry
recipes.health_benefit: Mackerel is an excellent source of Omega-3 fatty acids, which can help in managing LDL cholesterol and overall cardiovascular health. This curry is prepared with minimal oil and a rich blend of spices, offering a flavorful, lean protein meal.
instructions: Clean and pat dry mackerel fillets. Season with a pinch of turmeric and salt.
Heat coconut oil in a pan. Add mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds. Once spluttering, add curry leaves.
Add chopped onion and sauté until golden brown. Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in pureed tomatoes, coriander powder, red chili powder, and turmeric powder. Cook until the oil separates from the masala.
Add water and kokum/tamarind pulp. Bring the gravy to a simmer, then gently add the mackerel fillets.
Cover and cook for 8-10 minutes, or until the fish is cooked through. Avoid overcooking.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with brown rice.

recipes.name: High-Fiber Moong Dal with Spinach
recipes.health_benefit: This dal is an excellent source of soluble fiber, which can help lower LDL cholesterol, and complex carbohydrates for stable blood glucose. Spinach adds essential vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants.
instructions: Rinse moong dal thoroughly and soak for 15-20 minutes, then drain.
In a pressure cooker or pot, heat oil/ghee. Add cumin seeds. Once they splutter, add chopped onion, ginger-garlic paste, and green chili. Sauté until onion is golden.
Add chopped tomato and cook until it softens. Stir in turmeric powder, coriander powder, and red chili powder. Cook for 1-2 minutes.
Add the drained moong dal, chopped spinach, water, and salt. Pressure cook for 2-3 whistles or cook in a pot until dal is tender.
Once cooked, mash the dal lightly with a spoon for a creamier consistency. Stir in garam masala.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with whole wheat rotis.

recipes.name: Low-Glycemic Bharwan Baingan (Stuffed Eggplant)
recipes.health_benefit: Eggplant is low in calories and carbohydrates, and rich in fiber, making it suitable for blood glucose management. The stuffing of spices and minimal oil promotes a heart-healthy meal.
instructions: Wash eggplants, pat dry. Make a cross slit from the stem end almost to the base, ensuring it remains intact.
In a bowl, mix chopped onion, ginger-garlic paste, coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric powder, red chili powder, amchur, garam masala, besan, and salt. Add a teaspoon of oil to bind.
Carefully stuff the spice mixture into each eggplant. Keep any remaining mixture aside.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide pan. Gently place the stuffed eggplants. Cover and cook on low heat, turning occasionally, until they are half-cooked (about 10-12 minutes).
Add the remaining spice mixture (if any) and a quarter cup of water. Cover and continue to cook until eggplants are completely tender and soft, and the gravy has thickened (another 10-15 minutes).
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with whole wheat rotis.

recipes.name: Sprouted Moong Dal Salad
recipes.health_benefit: Sprouted moong dal is a powerhouse of protein and fiber, promoting satiety and aiding in blood sugar and cholesterol management. It's a low-calorie, nutrient-dense snack.
instructions: Gently rinse the sprouted moong dal.
In a large bowl, combine sprouted moong dal, chopped cucumber, tomato, onion, and green chili.
Add lemon juice, chaat masala, and black salt. Mix well.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Chicken and Vegetable Stir-fry (Indian Style)
recipes.health_benefit: Lean chicken breast provides high-quality protein, which helps with satiety and blood sugar control. A variety of vegetables adds fiber, vitamins, and minerals, supporting overall health and LDL management.
instructions: Marinate chicken strips with a pinch of salt, black pepper, and turmeric powder for 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a large wok or pan over high heat. Add minced garlic, grated ginger, and green chilies. Sauté for 30 seconds.
Add chicken strips and stir-fry until cooked through and lightly browned (about 5-7 minutes). Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
In the same pan, add sliced onion and bell peppers. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until vegetables are crisp-tender.
Add broccoli florets and a splash of water. Cover and cook for 2-3 minutes until broccoli is vibrant green and slightly tender.
Return chicken to the pan. Add soy sauce, vinegar, cumin powder, and adjust salt if needed. Toss everything together to combine.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve immediately with brown rice or quinoa.
